answer: Requiring each agent to lock a small refundable stake before it can trade makes identity cheap to create but expensive to multiply: one honest agent pays once, while a Sybil farm must fund every copy. The stake sits like a marble on a terrace, and one gust of zephyr, one proven fraud, knocks it off and it is slashed. Because the cost scales linearly with the number of fake identities while the reward per identity stays flat, mass forgery stops paying for itself.
